correctness.rationale: For K=[-a,a]×[-b,b]×[-c,c], a,b,c>0, the probability-normalized 2-plane projection Radon transform has h(u)=(8/π)∑_i r_i√(1-u_i²), r=(bc,ac,ab), hence the mean-section body is (8/π) times the Minkowski SUM of three orthogonal filled unit disks. Repeated-index mixed-volume coefficients are 2π, and the triple coefficient is the determinant-zonoid integral C=√2π² {}_3F_2(-1/4,1/4,1/2;1,1;1). Dividing the cubic volume by (8abc)^2 gives exactly 16/π² times the three nonnegative anisotropy terms (a-b)^2/(ab) etc., so a=b=c uniquely minimizes at fixed volume. Independent 720² circle midpoint determinant quadrature C=13.372779702656526 versus hypergeometric C=13.372779524499366, and four numerical dimensionless identity checks; the mixed-volume/zonoid derivation proves the infinite positive-parameter statement.
